models.name: FLUX.1
models.summary: Black Forest Labs' rectified-flow transformer for text-to-image. schnell is the distilled, few-step, permissively-licensed variant; dev is the higher-quality full model under a non-commercial license. Run here through mflux (registry/runtimes/mflux.yaml), which quantizes and executes on Metal.

restrictions: non-commercial use only (see LICENSE.md on the model card)
output usage restrictions apply per the license text
no redistribution of the weights outside the license terms

variants.name: FLUX.1 [schnell] (mflux, 4-bit)

download.note: Sum of the 13 files under text_encoder/, text_encoder_2/, transformer/ and vae/ (huggingface_hub.HfApi().model_info(files_metadata=True)) — the same subtree mflux's own download_patterns pulls. Excludes the 23.8 GB monolithic flux1-schnell.safetensors also hosted in this repo, which mflux never downloads. mflux quantizes weights after download, not before, so this figure is the same regardless of --quantize.

working_set.note: Estimated as download bytes (bf16 on disk, ~2 bytes/param) scaled by the int4/bf16 width ratio (4/16) plus a 10% activation margin: 33721097067 * 0.25 * 1.1. Not measured — mflux quantizes the transformer and both text encoders on load (any module exposing to_quantized, per quantization_predicate in flux_weight_definition.py), so resident size should track this closely, but nobody has run Activity Monitor against it yet.

variants.notes: Distilled, timestep-guided model designed for 2-4 sampling steps (source: FLUX.1-schnell model card). --quantize 4 with mflux-generate. Verified against black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell via HfApi 2026-08-22; alias "schnell" confirmed live in mflux-capabilities 0.19.0 output.

variants.name: FLUX.1 [schnell] (mflux, 8-bit)

download.note: Same subtree as flux-schnell-4bit — one repo, one download, quantization happens locally after the fetch. See that variant's note for the exact file list and how it was confirmed against mflux's download_patterns.

working_set.note: Estimated as download bytes scaled by the int8/bf16 width ratio (8/16) plus a 10% activation margin: 33721097067 * 0.5 * 1.1. Same caveat as the 4-bit variant — derived from the quantization ratio, not measured against a running process.

variants.notes: Same weights as flux-schnell-4bit, --quantize 8. Fits a 32 GB Mac with real headroom; the 4-bit variant exists for machines with less to spare or when speed matters more than the extra fidelity.

variants.name: FLUX.1 [dev] (mflux, bf16)

download.note: Same file-pattern methodology as the schnell variants, summed against black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev instead (13 files, same subtree layout).

working_set.note: Unquantized bf16 run: download bytes (already bf16 on disk) plus a 10% activation margin, no quantization ratio applied: 33741557618 * 1.1. Included for contrast against the two quantized schnell variants above — at ~37 GB resident this does not comfortably fit a 32 GB Mac, which is the whole point of quantizing schnell in the first place.

restrictions: non-commercial use only (see LICENSE.md on the model card)
output usage restrictions apply per the license text
no redistribution of the weights outside the license terms

variants.notes: Full-quality, non-distilled model; the model card recommends 20-50 steps and CFG guidance schnell does not use. --quantize omitted (mflux-generate --model dev with no --quantize flag). Non-commercial license — do not ship generated output from a commercial product without checking LICENSE.md. Verified against black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev via HfApi 2026-08-22; alias "dev" confirmed live in mflux-capabilities 0.19.0 output.

variants.name: FLUX.2 [klein-4B] (mflux, 4-bit)

download.note: Sum of 16 files (huggingface_hub.HfApi().model_info(files_metadata=True)) under vae/, transformer/, text_encoder/, tokenizer/, plus added_tokens.json and chat_template.jinja -- matches mflux's own download_patterns. Excludes the 7.75 GB monolithic flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors also hosted in this repo, which mflux never downloads.

working_set.note: mflux's own "Peak MLX memory: 10.52 GB" line, printed by mflux-generate-flux2 --model flux2-klein-4b --quantize 4 --steps 4 --height 512 --width 512 at the end of a real run on this Mac (10.52 * 1024**3 bytes). This is mlx.metal's own peak-allocation counter, not an OS RSS estimate. See registry/measurements/ apple-m1-max-32gb/flux2-klein-4b-4bit/ for the paired load_seconds and seconds_per_image samples from the same driver run; this is the one working_set number in this file that is not a paper estimate.

variants.notes: This repo (black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B) is NOT gated and is apache-2.0 -- unlike FLUX.1-schnell/dev above, both of which require accepting a license gate on huggingface.co before the weights can be downloaded at all, which this session could not do (accepting a HuggingFace model gate is an account action requiring the user's own browser session). This variant is the one actually exercised for the real load/generate measurement recorded for this task -- see registry/measurements/. --quantize 4 with mflux-generate-flux2. Verified against black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B via HfApi 2026-08-22; alias "flux2-klein-4b" confirmed live in mflux-capabilities 0.19.0 output.

models.name: LTX Video
models.summary: Fast and good, and not open source. The repo carries every checkpoint ever shipped, so fetching it whole is 236 GB against the few gigabytes actually wanted.

restrictions: Free only while your annual revenue is under $10M
The terms pass to anyone you ship it to

working_set.note: transformer weights plus text encoder and VAE held resident, no measured run on any machine yet

restrictions: Free only while your annual revenue is under $10M
The terms pass to anyone you ship it to

speed.note: 121 frames at 512x512 in 11 seconds, reported at https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-Video/discussions/6 and converted at the model card's 30 FPS. The source does not say which checkpoint or precision was used, so this may not be this exact variant — treat it as the speed class of a small LTX model on a 4090, not as this row's number.

variants.name: LTX Video 13B 0.9.8 distilled FP8

working_set.note: transformer weights plus text encoder and VAE held resident, no measured run on any machine yet

restrictions: Free only while your annual revenue is under $10M
The terms pass to anyone you ship it to

speed.note: 88 frames at 1216x704 in 2 minutes 8 seconds without CPU offloading, reported at https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Video/issues/166 and converted at the model card's 30 FPS. The report says "13B model" without stating distilled or fp8, and the card is a modified 48 GB 4090, so this is an upper bound for a 13B LTX rather than this variant's figure.

variants.notes: FP8 has no Metal path and fails rather than falling back, so this is CUDA on Ada or newer. Reported independently at https://lilting.ch/en/articles/ltx2-wan22-mac-local-video-gen

models.name: Wan 2.1
models.summary: Alibaba's text-to-video family. The 1.3B is the smallest genuinely open video model that is worth running.

working_set.note: 8.19 GB peak GPU memory, stated on the official model card at https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B for a 5-second 480p generation. Replaces our earlier 11 GB estimate; the card is describing the same bf16 weights this variant downloads.

speed.note: About 4 minutes for a 5-second 480p clip, stated on the official model card at https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B without quantisation or other optimisation. Not measured by us.

models.name: Wan 2.2
models.summary: The only video model here under a licence with no revenue cap and no territory exclusion. That makes it the safe default even where it is not the fastest.

working_set.note: transformer weights plus text encoder and VAE held resident, no measured run on any machine yet

speed.note: 82 minutes for a 2-second clip in GGUF, reported at https://lilting.ch/en/articles/ltx2-wan22-mac-local-video-gen — third-party, on twice the memory of a 32 GB machine. Not measured by us. Treat as the order of magnitude, not the number.
